verse: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
story: Two men go up to the temple to pray, and Jesus surprises His hearers by making the despised tax collector the hero of the story.

The Pharisee stands near and lists his virtues. The tax collector stays back, eyes down, striking his chest as if the trouble lives there. He brings no record at all, only a plea. The word he uses for mercy comes from the temple's sacrifices: be atoned toward me, the sinner. He asks God to deal with his sin in the one way he cannot. Jesus says this man, not the other, went home justified, counted righteous by God's mercy alone.
Lent is not a season for polishing our record before God. Come as you are today, with nothing in your hands, and ask for the mercy He gives.
theme: Lent: repentance, the road to the cross
